correctness.rationale: For the specified integral model, differentiation gives the Hessian scalar -54, a unit at 7. Independent exact arithmetic gives the mod-7 affine resultant -y(y-2)^21 and specialized common factors z and (z-4)^2. The line X=0 adds only the other two coordinate vertices. There is no common component, and at each vertex the two local linear terms are independent. Bezout therefore gives 24-3=21 at [1:2:4]. The gradient equations in characteristic 7 force Y^7=2 in X=1 and then Z=4; direct substitution verifies singularity. In the projective ambient local rings above 7, the uniformizer followed by the two equations is a regular sequence at the common zeros; permutation gives no 7-torsion in the quotient, hence flatness over the DVR. Properness and the zero-dimensional special fiber imply finiteness. Over Q, the determinant of multiplication by h on Q[y,z]/(f), in the basis 1,z,z^2, independently gives a degree-22 polynomial with gcd 1 with its derivative. Its root valuations count the local lengths of the finite affine quotient (cokernel of that multiplication), so all 22 are simple. The two coordinate points at infinity are transverse. The generic Klein quartic is smooth: the three nonzero-coordinate gradient equations would multiply to 1=(-3)^3, and a zero coordinate would force all three zero. Thus the generic points are classical flexes. The special length is not an intrinsic flex order.
